sanskrit.deva:
तं तथा कृपयाविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् ।
विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam |
viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ || 1 ||

padaccheda.iast: tam tathā kṛpayā āviṣṭam aśru-pūrṇa-ākula-īkṣaṇam viṣīdantam idam vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तम् तथा कृपया आविष्टम् अश्रु-पूर्ण-आकुल-ईक्षणम् विषीदन्तम् इदम् वाक्यम् उवाच मधुसूदनः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

words.meaning: whose troubled eyes were filled with tears

translations.text: Saṃjaya said: To him who was thus overcome by compassion, despairing, his troubled eyes filled with tears, Madhusūdana spoke these words:

sanskrit.deva:
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam |
anāryajuṣṭam asvargyam akīrtikaram arjuna || 2 ||

lines.iast: kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam

padaccheda.iast: kutaḥ tvā kaśmalam idam viṣame samupasthitam an-ārya-juṣṭam a-svargyam a-kīrti-karam arjuna
padaccheda.deva: कुतः त्वा कश्मलम् इदम् विषमे समुपस्थितम् अन्-आर्य-जुष्टम् अ-स्वर्ग्यम् अ-कीर्ति-करम् अर्जुन

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: The Blessed Lord said: Whence has this faintness of heart come upon you at this time of crisis, O Arjuna? It is unworthy of a noble man, it does not lead to heaven, and it brings disgrace.

sanskrit.deva:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परंतप ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate |
kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha paraṃtapa || 3 ||

lines.iast: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate
lines.deva: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते

padaccheda.iast: klaibyam mā sma gamaḥ pārtha na etat tvayi upapadyate kṣudram hṛdaya-daurbalyam tyaktvā uttiṣṭha paraṃtapa
padaccheda.deva: क्लैब्यम् मा स्म गमः पार्थ न एतत् त्वयि उपपद्यते क्षुद्रम् हृदय-दौर्बल्यम् त्यक्त्वा उत्तिष्ठ परंतप

translations.text: Do not yield to unmanliness, O Pārtha; it does not befit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and arise, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit.deva:
कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana |
iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv arisūdana || 4 ||

lines.iast: kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana
lines.deva: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन

padaccheda.iast: katham bhīṣmam aham saṃkhye droṇam ca madhusūdana iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjā-arhau ari-sūdana
padaccheda.deva: कथम् भीष्मम् अहम् संख्ये द्रोणम् च मधुसूदन इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजा-अर्हौ अरि-सूदन

translations.text: Arjuna said: How shall I fight in battle with arrows against Bhīṣma and Droṇa, O Madhusūdana, who are worthy of worship, O slayer of enemies?

sanskrit.deva:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावाञ्श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्षमपीह लोके ।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान्रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvāñśreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣamapīha loke |
hatvārthakāmāṃstu gurūnihaiva bhuñjīya bhogānrudhirapradigdhān || 5 ||

lines.iast: gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvāñśreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣamapīha loke
lines.deva: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावाञ्श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्षमपीह लोके

padaccheda.iast: gurūn a-hatvā hi mahā-anubhāvān śreyaḥ bhoktum bhaikṣam api iha loke hatvā artha-kāmān tu gurūn iha eva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān
padaccheda.deva: गुरून् अ-हत्वा हि महा-अनुभावान् श्रेयः भोक्तुम् भैक्षम् अपि इह लोके हत्वा अर्थ-कामान् तु गुरून् इह एव भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिर-प्रदिग्धान्

translations.text: It is better to live in this world even on food got by begging than to kill these teachers of great dignity. If I killed my teachers, though they seek their own gain, I should enjoy here only pleasures smeared with blood.

sanskrit.deva:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ |
yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāmaste 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
lines.deva: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः

lines.iast: yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāmaste 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
lines.deva: यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः

padaccheda.iast: na ca etat vidmaḥ katarat naḥ garīyaḥ yat vā jayema yadi vā naḥ jayeyuḥ yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmaḥ te avasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
padaccheda.deva: न च एतत् विद्मः कतरत् नः गरीयः यत् वा जयेम यदि वा नः जयेयुः यान् एव हत्वा न जिजीविषामः ते अवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: We do not know which is better for us: that we should conquer them, or that they should conquer us. The very sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, after killing whom we would not wish to live, stand before us.

notes: jijīviṣāmaḥ is a desiderative form; it is labelled here as a present.

sanskrit.deva:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः ।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasaṃmūḍhacetāḥ |
yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme śiṣyaste 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam || 7 ||

lines.iast: yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme śiṣyaste 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
lines.deva: यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्

padaccheda.iast: kārpaṇya-doṣa-upahata-svabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvām dharma-saṃmūḍha-cetāḥ yat śreyaḥ syāt niścitam brūhi tat me śiṣyaḥ te aham śādhi mām tvām prapannam
padaccheda.deva: कार्पण्य-दोष-उपहत-स्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वाम् धर्म-संमूढ-चेताः यत् श्रेयः स्यात् निश्चितम् ब्रूहि तत् मे शिष्यः ते अहम् शाधि माम् त्वाम् प्रपन्नम्

words.meaning: my nature overcome by the fault of faint-heartedness

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: My nature is overcome by the fault of faint-heartedness, and my mind is confused about dharma. I ask you: tell me for certain what is better. I am your pupil; instruct me, who have taken refuge in you.

sanskrit.deva:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyādyacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām |
avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam || 8 ||

padaccheda.iast: na hi prapaśyāmi mama apanudyāt yat śokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām avāpya bhūmau asapatnam ṛddham rājyam surāṇām api ca ādhipatyam
padaccheda.deva: न हि प्रपश्यामि मम अपनुद्यात् यत् शोकम् उच्छोषणम् इन्द्रियाणाम् अवाप्य भूमौ असपत्नम् ऋद्धम् राज्यम् सुराणाम् अपि च आधिपत्यम्

translations.text: For I do not see what would dispel this grief that dries up my senses, even if I obtained an unrivalled and prosperous kingdom on earth, and lordship over the gods.

sanskrit.deva:
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परंतप ।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ paraṃtapa |
na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha || 9 ||

lines.iast: na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
lines.deva: न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह

padaccheda.iast: evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśam guḍākeśaḥ paraṃtapa na yotsye iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīm babhūva ha
padaccheda.deva: एवम् उक्त्वा हृषीकेशम् गुडाकेशः परंतप न योत्स्ये इति गोविन्दम् उक्त्वा तूष्णीम् बभूव ह

translations.text: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hṛṣīkeśa, O scorcher of foes, Guḍākeśa said to Govinda, “I will not fight”, and fell silent.

notes: The critical edition reads paraṃtapa, a vocative addressed to Dhṛtarāṣṭra. The commonly recited text has paraṃtapaḥ, a nominative describing Arjuna.

sanskrit.deva:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata |
senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṃ vacaḥ || 10 ||

lines.iast: tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata
senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṃ vacaḥ

padaccheda.iast: tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasan iva bhārata senayoḥ ubhayoḥ madhye viṣīdantam idam vacaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तम् उवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन् इव भारत सेनयोः उभयोः मध्ये विषीदन्तम् इदम् वचः

translations.text: To him who was despairing there between the two armies, O Bhārata, Hṛṣīkeśa, as though smiling, spoke these words:

notes: Śaṅkara's commentary begins here. The passage from 1.2 up to ‘I will not fight’ shows, he says, how grief and delusion, the seed of the cycle of birth and death, arise in living beings. Seeing that Arjuna, sunk in a sea of grief, could be lifted out by nothing but knowledge of the Self, the Lord begins that teaching. The settled meaning of the Gītā, he holds, is that liberation comes from knowledge of the truth alone, not from knowledge combined with action.

sanskrit.deva:
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase |
gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ || 11 ||

padaccheda.iast: a-śocyān anvaśocaḥ tvam prajñā-vādān ca bhāṣase gatāsūn a-gatāsūn ca na anuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
padaccheda.deva: अ-शोच्यान् अन्वशोचः त्वम् प्रज्ञा-वादान् च भाषसे गतासून् अ-गतासून् च न अनुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः

words.meaning: those who are not to be grieved for

translations.text: The Blessed Lord said: You have grieved for those who are not to be grieved for, and yet you speak the words of the wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: the text from 1.2 to 2.9 is to be read as showing how grief and delusion, the seed of the cycle of birth and death, arise. Arjuna's grief and delusion come from the mistaken notions ‘I am theirs, they are mine’ about kingdom, teachers, sons, friends and kinsmen. His discernment overpowered by them, he turned away from battle, his own dharma as a warrior, and set about another's, living on alms. So do all beings whose minds are seized by grief and delusion give up their own dharma and take to what is forbidden; and even their action in their own dharma is done with desire for its fruit and with the sense of ‘I’, so that dharma and adharma pile up and the cycle does not cease. Grief and delusion cease by nothing other than knowledge of the Self preceded by the renunciation of all action; wishing to teach that, the Lord makes Arjuna the occasion, for the good of all.

Śaṅkara then sets out and rejects the view that liberation comes not from steadfastness in knowledge alone but from knowledge joined with Vedic and smṛti rites. His grounds: the Lord speaks of two separate understandings, the Sāṃkhya (2.11–31, the truth of the Self, which is no doer) and Yoga (the practice of the means before that understanding is born), and of two paths resting on them (2.39, 3.3), because knowledge and action, resting on the notions of non-doer and doer, of one and many, cannot be in one man at once; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka likewise enjoins rites for the man of desire and renunciation for him who wants only the Self. Arjuna's question at 3.1–2 (‘if you hold understanding better than action … tell me the one’) would make no sense had both been taught together, as no one told to eat what is sweet and cool asks which of the two cures bile; and the Lord's answer, ‘two paths were taught by me’, would not fit.

Śaṅkara: when one who knows the truth still acts, for the holding together of the world, that is not action that could be joined with knowledge: like the Lord's own conduct as a warrior, it is without the sense of ‘I’ and without aim at its fruit. ‘Janaka and others reached perfection by action alone’ (3.20) means either that, being knowers, they reached it without giving up action, or, if they were not knowers, that by action offered to the Lord they reached purity of mind or the rise of knowledge. So the settled sense of the Gītā is that liberation is from knowledge of the truth alone, not from knowledge joined with action. Seeing no rescue for Arjuna, sunk in a sea of grief, but knowledge of the Self, the Lord in compassion begins.

Śaṅkara: Bhīṣma, Droṇa and the others are not to be grieved for, because their conduct is good and because in their true nature they are eternal. The paṇḍitas are the knowers of the Self: paṇḍā is the understanding that has the Self for its object. Arjuna shows foolishness and learning together, like one out of his mind.

sanskrit.deva:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ |
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param || 12 ||

lines.iast: na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ
lines.deva: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः

lines.iast: na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
lines.deva: न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्

padaccheda.iast: na tu eva aham jātu na āsam na tvam na ime janādhipāḥ na ca eva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param
padaccheda.deva: न तु एव अहम् जातु न आसम् न त्वम् न इमे जनाधिपाः न च एव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयम् अतः परम्

translations.text: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these rulers of men; nor shall any of us ever cease to be hereafter.

notes: Śaṅkara: in all three times we are eternal in our nature as the Self, as space is through the making and breaking of pots. The plural follows the difference of bodies; it is not meant to teach that there are many selves.

sanskrit.deva:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dehino 'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā |
tathā dehāntaraprāptir dhīrastatra na muhyati || 13 ||

padaccheda.iast: dehinaḥ asmin yathā dehe kaumāram yauvanam jarā tathā deha-antara-prāptiḥ dhīraḥ tatra na muhyati
padaccheda.deva: देहिनः अस्मिन् यथा देहे कौमारम् यौवनम् जरा तथा देह-अन्तर-प्राप्तिः धीरः तत्र न मुह्यति

translations.text: As the embodied Self passes in this body through childhood, youth and old age, so it passes to another body. The wise man is not deluded by that.

notes: Śaṅkara: the Self does not perish when one stage ends nor is it born when the next begins; without changing, it gains each stage, and in the same way another body.

sanskrit.deva:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ |
āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṃstitikṣasva bhārata || 14 ||

padaccheda.iast: mātrā-sparśāḥ tu kaunteya śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ āgama-apāyinaḥ anityāḥ tān titikṣasva bhārata
padaccheda.deva: मात्रा-स्पर्शाः तु कौन्तेय शीत-उष्ण-सुख-दुःख-दाः आगम-अपायिनः अनित्याः तान् तितिक्षस्व भारत

words.meaning: which give cold and heat, pleasure and pain

translations.text: The contacts of the senses with their objects, O son of Kuntī, give cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, and do not last. Endure them, O Bhārata.

notes: Śaṅkara: mātrāḥ are the senses, by which sound and the other objects are measured; their sparśāḥ are contacts with those objects. Or else sparśāḥ are the objects themselves. Cold and heat are named apart because each is sometimes pleasant and sometimes painful, whereas pleasure and pain are fixed in nature. To endure them is neither to rejoice nor to despair over them.
titikṣasva is a desiderative form; it is labelled here as an imperative.

sanskrit.deva:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha |
samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate || 15 ||

lines.iast: yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
lines.deva: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ

padaccheda.iast: yam hi na vyathayanti ete puruṣam puruṣa-ṛṣabha sama-duḥkha-sukham dhīram saḥ amṛta-tvāya kalpate
padaccheda.deva: यम् हि न व्यथयन्ति एते पुरुषम् पुरुष-ऋषभ सम-दुःख-सुखम् धीरम् सः अमृत-त्वाय कल्पते

words.meaning: the same in pain and pleasure

translations.text: The wise man whom these do not trouble, O best of men, who is the same in pain and pleasure: he is fit for immortality.

notes: Śaṅkara: he is not shaken because he sees the eternal Self. Immortality here is liberation.

sanskrit.deva:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ |
ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo 'ntastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ || 16 ||

lines.iast: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
lines.deva: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः

padaccheda.iast: na asataḥ vidyate bhāvaḥ na abhāvaḥ vidyate sataḥ ubhayoḥ api dṛṣṭaḥ antaḥ tu anayoḥ tattva-darśibhiḥ
padaccheda.deva: न असतः विद्यते भावः न अभावः विद्यते सतः उभयोः अपि दृष्टः अन्तः तु अनयोः तत्त्व-दर्शिभिः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: by those who see the truth

translations.text: The unreal has no being, and the real never ceases to be. The truth about both has been seen by those who see things as they are.

notes: Śaṅkara: the unreal is cold, heat and the like, with their causes: every effect, being a modification that is never found apart from its cause, as a pot is never found apart from clay. That of which the awareness never fails is real; that of which it fails is unreal. In ‘the pot is’, ‘the cloth is’, the awareness of pot and cloth comes and goes, the awareness of being does not. The real is the Self.

Śaṅkara: anta is the settled conclusion, that the real is only real and the unreal only unreal. In tattva, ‘that’ (tad) is a name of Brahman, which is all; tattva is its true nature. Taking the view of those who see it, Arjuna is to endure the pairs of opposites, knowing them to appear falsely, like water in a mirage.

sanskrit.deva:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati || 17 ||

lines.iast: avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
lines.deva: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्

padaccheda.iast: a-vināśi tu tat viddhi yena sarvam idam tatam vināśam avyayasya asya na kaścit kartum arhati
padaccheda.deva: अ-विनाशि तु तत् विद्धि येन सर्वम् इदम् ततम् विनाशम् अव्ययस्य अस्य न कश्चित् कर्तुम् अर्हति

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. No one can bring about the destruction of this undecaying one.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘that’ is Brahman, called the real, which pervades this whole world, space included, as space pervades pots. It is undecaying: having no parts and nothing of its own to lose, it neither grows nor lessens. Not even the Lord can destroy the Self, for the Self is Brahman, and an action cannot be turned upon oneself.

sanskrit.deva:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
anāśino 'prameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata || 18 ||

padaccheda.iast: antavantaḥ ime dehāḥ nityasya uktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ a-nāśinaḥ a-prameyasya tasmāt yudhyasva bhārata
padaccheda.deva: अन्तवन्तः इमे देहाः नित्यस्य उक्ताः शरीरिणः अ-नाशिनः अ-प्रमेयस्य तस्मात् युध्यस्व भारत

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: These bodies of the eternal embodied Self, which is indestructible and beyond measure, are said to have an end. Therefore fight, O Bhārata.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘eternal’ and ‘indestructible’ are not a repetition; the two words deny both kinds of perishing, complete disappearance and change into another state. aprameya: not to be determined by perception and the other means of knowledge, for the Self is self-established; scripture is a means of knowing it only in that it removes what is wrongly laid upon it.

Śaṅkara: ‘therefore fight’ does not enjoin fighting. Arjuna had already taken up the battle and had stopped through grief and delusion; the Lord only removes that obstacle. The words restate what was already so; they are not a command.

sanskrit.deva:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam |
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate || 19 ||

lines.iast: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam
lines.deva: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्

lines.iast: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
lines.deva: उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ enam vetti hantāram yaḥ ca enam manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānītaḥ na ayam hanti na hanyate
padaccheda.deva: यः एनम् वेत्ति हन्तारम् यः च एनम् मन्यते हतम् उभौ तौ न विजानीतः न अयम् हन्ति न हन्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: He who thinks this Self a slayer, and he who thinks it slain: neither of the two knows. It does not slay, nor is it slain.

notes: Śaṅkara: this verse and the next are brought in from the Veda as witnesses (compare Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.2.19 and 18). The Self is neither the agent nor the object of the act of killing, because it does not change.

sanskrit.deva:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ |
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre || 20 ||

lines.iast: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
lines.deva: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः

lines.iast: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
lines.deva: अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे

padaccheda.iast: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācit na ayam bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ ajaḥ nityaḥ śāśvataḥ ayam purāṇaḥ na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
padaccheda.deva: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचित् न अयम् भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः अजः नित्यः शाश्वतः अयम् पुराणः न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे

translations.text: It is never born, nor does it ever die; nor, having been, does it ever cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.

notes: Śaṅkara divides the words as bhūtvā abhavitā: ‘having been, it does not afterwards become non-existent’, so it does not die; and, taking vā and na again, ‘not having been, it does not come to be’, so it is not born. The word analysis above gives the undivided bhavitā.

Śaṅkara: the verse denies in the Self the six changes that worldly things undergo. Birth and death are denied outright; śāśvata denies decline, purāṇa (‘new even of old’) denies growth, and na hanyate, where han means ‘to be transformed’, denies transformation.

sanskrit.deva:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् ।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam |
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam || 21 ||

lines.iast: vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
lines.deva: कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्

padaccheda.iast: veda a-vināśinam nityam yaḥ enam ajam avyayam katham saḥ puruṣaḥ pārtha kam ghātayati hanti kam
padaccheda.deva: वेद अ-विनाशिनम् नित्यम् यः एनम् अजम् अव्ययम् कथम् सः पुरुषः पार्थ कम् घातयति हन्ति कम्

words.meaning: does he cause to be slain

translations.text: He who knows this Self to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and undecaying: how, O Pārtha, does that man slay anyone, or cause anyone to be slain?

notes: DCS has no entry for the first half-line (vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam); its words have no analysis yet.

Śaṅkara: avināśin is free of the last change of state, destruction; nitya, of transformation; aja, of birth; avyaya, of decline. The question is a denial: he slays no one in any way and causes no one to be slain. Killing is only an example: since the reason given, changelessness, holds equally everywhere, what the Lord means is that every action is denied for the knower.

Śaṅkara: it may be objected that one who knows a changeless post can still act. But here the knower is the Self itself; knowing does not belong to the aggregate of body and organs, so what is left is that the uncompounded, changeless Self is the knower. As the Self, changeless all the while, is imagined through ignorance to be the perceiver of sound and the rest that the understanding brings, because it is not told apart from the activity of the understanding, so it is called ‘knower’ through the knowledge that tells Self from not-Self, which is also an activity of the understanding and not ultimately real. The actions that scripture enjoins are therefore enjoined for one who does not know.

Śaṅkara: nor can it be said that knowledge too is enjoined only for one who does not know, so that there is no difference. When the sense of an injunction such as the agnihotra is understood, something remains to be performed by one who thinks ‘I am the doer, this is my duty’; when the sense of ‘it is not born’ is understood, nothing remains to be performed: only the knowledge ‘I am not the doer, not the enjoyer’ arises. So the knower who sees the changeless Self, and the seeker of liberation, are entitled only to the renunciation of all action. Hence the two paths of 3.3, the two ways Vyāsa taught his son (Mahābhārata, Śāntiparvan), and 3.27–28 and 5.13.

Śaṅkara: some who think themselves learned say that the knowledge ‘I am the one Self, changeless, not a doer, free of the six changes beginning with birth’ arises in no one. Then the teaching ‘it is not born’ would be pointless. If scripture gives knowledge of dharma and adharma and of the doer's passage to another body, why not of that same Self's changelessness? Nor is the Self beyond every instrument: ‘by the mind alone it is to be seen’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.19); the mind refined by scripture, the teacher's instruction, calm and restraint is the instrument for seeing it. Knowledge, once arisen, necessarily removes the contrary ignorance shown in 2.19; and to be the doer, the object or the prompter of an action is the work of ignorance in every action alike.

Śaṅkara, on 5.13, ‘having renounced all actions with the mind’: this is not limited to mental actions, since speech and body act only after the mind; nor does it leave out the mental causes of scriptural actions, since the verse adds ‘neither acting nor causing to act’; nor is it said of a dying man, since he ‘sits in the city of nine gates’; nor can it be construed ‘laying actions down in the body’, since sitting needs a place and renouncing does not, and saṃnyāsa here means giving up, not depositing. So in the Gītā the knower of the Self is entitled to renunciation alone, not to action.
The DCS gives no analysis for the first line of this verse; the analysis here is ours.

sanskrit.deva:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi |
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī || 22 ||

lines.iast: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi
lines.deva: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि

lines.iast: tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
lines.deva: तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही

padaccheda.iast: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naraḥ aparāṇi tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāni anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
padaccheda.deva: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरः अपराणि तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णानि अन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. pl.
past passive participle n. acc. pl.

translations.text: As a man casts off worn-out clothes and takes other, new ones, so the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies and goes to other, new ones.

notes: Śaṅkara: the embodied Self does so without itself changing, just as the man does.

sanskrit.deva:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ |
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ || 23 ||

lines.iast: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
lines.deva: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः

lines.iast: na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
lines.deva: न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः

padaccheda.iast: na enam chindanti śastrāṇi na enam dahati pāvakaḥ na ca enam kledayanti āpaḥ na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
padaccheda.deva: न एनम् छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि न एनम् दहति पावकः न च एनम् क्लेदयन्ति आपः न शोषयति मारुतः

translations.text: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, waters do not wet it, and wind does not dry it.

notes: Śaṅkara: having no parts, it cannot be divided by a sword, reduced to ash, loosened by moisture or dried out.

sanskrit.deva:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca |
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ || 24 ||

padaccheda.iast: a-chedyaḥ ayam a-dāhyaḥ ayam a-kledyaḥ a-śoṣyaḥ eva ca nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇuḥ acalaḥ ayam sanātanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अ-छेद्यः अयम् अ-दाह्यः अयम् अ-क्लेद्यः अ-शोष्यः एव च नित्यः सर्व-गतः स्थाणुः अचलः अयम् सनातनः

translations.text: It cannot be cut, burnt, wetted or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable and ancient.

notes: Śaṅkara: since those things, which destroy one another, cannot destroy it, it is eternal; being eternal it is all-pervading; being all-pervading it is stable, like a post; being stable it is immovable; and so it is ancient, not produced from any cause. The same thing is said again in other words because the Self is hard to understand.

sanskrit.deva:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते ।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yamucyate |
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi || 25 ||

padaccheda.iast: avyaktaḥ ayam a-cintyaḥ ayam a-vikāryaḥ ayam ucyate tasmāt evam viditvā enam na anuśocitum arhasi
padaccheda.deva: अव्यक्तः अयम् अ-चिन्त्यः अयम् अ-विकार्यः अयम् उच्यते तस्मात् एवम् विदित्वा एनम् न अनुशोचितुम् अर्हसि

translations.text: It is said to be unmanifest, unthinkable and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing it to be so, you ought not to grieve.

notes: Śaṅkara: unmanifest, because it is no object of any sense; and for that reason unthinkable, since only what the senses reach becomes an object of thought; unchangeable, unlike milk, which turns to curd.

sanskrit.deva:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam |
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho nainaṃ śocitumarhasi || 26 ||

lines.iast: atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam
lines.deva: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्

padaccheda.iast: atha ca enam nitya-jātam nityam vā manyase mṛtam tathā api tvam mahā-bāho na enam śocitum arhasi
padaccheda.deva: अथ च एनम् नित्य-जातम् नित्यम् वा मन्यसे मृतम् तथा अपि त्वम् महा-बाहो न एनम् शोचितुम् अर्हसि

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: But even if you think of it as constantly born and constantly dying, even so, O mighty-armed, you ought not to grieve for it.

notes: Śaṅkara: this is said granting, for the sake of argument, that the Self is impermanent: born with each body that arises and dying with each that perishes, as people commonly suppose.
The text of the bhāṣya reads naivam, ‘not thus’, where the critical edition has nainam.

sanskrit.deva:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ २७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi || 27 ||

lines.iast: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca
lines.deva: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च

padaccheda.iast: jātasya hi dhruvaḥ mṛtyuḥ dhruvam janma mṛtasya ca tasmāt a-parihārye arthe na tvam śocitum arhasi
padaccheda.deva: जातस्य हि ध्रुवः मृत्युः ध्रुवम् जन्म मृतस्य च तस्मात् अ-परिहार्ये अर्थे न त्वम् शोचितुम् अर्हसि

grammar.en: past passive participle m. gen. sg.
past passive participle m. gen. sg.

translations.text: For death is certain for one who is born, and birth is certain for one who has died. Therefore you ought not to grieve over what cannot be avoided.

sanskrit.deva:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ २८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata |
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā || 28 ||

padaccheda.iast: avyakta-ādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata avyakta-nidhanāni eva tatra kā paridevanā
padaccheda.deva: अव्यक्त-आदीनि भूतानि व्यक्त-मध्यानि भारत अव्यक्त-निधनानि एव तत्र का परिदेवना

translations.text: Beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in the middle, and unmanifest again in their end, O Bhārata. What is there in that to lament?

notes: Śaṅkara: the beings are the bodies and organs of sons, friends and the rest. avyakta here means ‘unseen’: before birth and after death they are not perceived. What lament can there be over beings that are an illusion: unseen, then seen, then gone?

sanskrit.deva:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥ २९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidenam āścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ |
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit || 29 ||

lines.iast: āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
lines.deva: आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्

padaccheda.iast: āścarya-vat paśyati kaścit enam āścarya-vat vadati tathā eva ca anyaḥ āścarya-vat ca enam anyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvā api enam veda na ca eva kaścit
padaccheda.deva: आश्चर्य-वत् पश्यति कश्चित् एनम् आश्चर्य-वत् वदति तथा एव च अन्यः आश्चर्य-वत् च एनम् अन्यः शृणोति श्रुत्वा अपि एनम् वेद न च एव कश्चित्

translations.text: One sees it as a wonder; another likewise speaks of it as a wonder; another hears of it as a wonder; and even having heard, no one knows it.

notes: Śaṅkara: a wonder is something strange, never seen before, that appears all at once. Or else the sense is that he who sees the Self is himself like a wonder, and so are he who speaks of it and he who hears: one among many thousands. So the Self is hard to understand.

sanskrit.deva:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत ।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥ ३० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata |
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi || 30 ||

lines.iast: dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata

padaccheda.iast: dehī nityam a-vadhyaḥ ayam dehe sarvasya bhārata tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvam śocitum arhasi
padaccheda.deva: देही नित्यम् अ-वध्यः अयम् देहे सर्वस्य भारत तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वम् शोचितुम् अर्हसि

translations.text: This embodied Self in the body of everyone can never be slain, O Bhārata. Therefore you ought not to grieve for any being.

notes: Śaṅkara: this sums up the section. Though the body of any creature is slain, the Self that dwells in it cannot be.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि ।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥ ३१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi |
dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo 'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate || 31 ||

padaccheda.iast: svadharmam api ca avekṣya na vikampitum arhasi dharmyāt hi yuddhāt śreyaḥ anyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate
padaccheda.deva: स्वधर्मम् अपि च अवेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुम् अर्हसि धर्म्यात् हि युद्धात् श्रेयः अन्यत् क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते

words.meaning: than one that accords with dharma

translations.text: Considering your own dharma too, you ought not to waver; for to a warrior there is nothing better than a war that accords with dharma.

notes: Śaṅkara: grief and delusion have been shown to be out of place in view of the highest truth; now the same is shown from the point of view of dharma. War is a warrior's natural dharma; waged for the sake of dharma and the protection of the people, through the conquest of the earth, it does not depart from dharma.

sanskrit.deva:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥ ३२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam |
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam || 32 ||

padaccheda.iast: yadṛcchayā ca upapannam svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam
padaccheda.deva: यदृच्छया च उपपन्नम् स्वर्ग-द्वारम् अपावृतम् सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धम् ईदृशम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.
past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: Fortunate are the warriors, O Pārtha, who obtain such a war, come unsought, an open gate to heaven.

sanskrit.deva:
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi |
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi || 33 ||

lines.iast: atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi
lines.deva: अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि

lines.iast: tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
lines.deva: ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि

padaccheda.iast: atha cet tvam imam dharmyam saṃgrāmam na kariṣyasi tataḥ svadharmam kīrtim ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi
padaccheda.deva: अथ चेत् त्वम् इमम् धर्म्यम् संग्रामम् न करिष्यसि ततः स्वधर्मम् कीर्तिम् च हित्वा पापम् अवाप्स्यसि

translations.text: But if you will not wage this battle, which accords with dharma, then, having abandoned your own dharma and your fame, you will incur sin.

notes: Śaṅkara: the fame is that which Arjuna won by his encounter with Mahādeva and the like.

sanskrit.deva:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् ।
संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥ ३४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te 'vyayām |
saṃbhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate || 34 ||

padaccheda.iast: akīrtim ca api bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te avyayām saṃbhāvitasya ca akīrtiḥ maraṇāt atiricyate
padaccheda.deva: अकीर्तिम् च अपि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति ते अव्ययाम् संभावितस्य च अकीर्तिः मरणात् अतिरिच्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. gen. sg.

words.meaning: for one who has been honoured

translations.text: People will also tell of your undying disgrace; and for one who has been honoured, disgrace is worse than death.

sanskrit.deva:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः ।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥ ३५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ |
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam || 35 ||

lines.iast: yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
lines.deva: येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्

padaccheda.iast: bhayāt raṇāt uparatam maṃsyante tvām mahā-rathāḥ yeṣām ca tvam bahu-mataḥ bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
padaccheda.deva: भयात् रणात् उपरतम् मंस्यन्ते त्वाम् महा-रथाः येषाम् च त्वम् बहु-मतः भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: The great chariot-warriors will think that you withdrew from the battle out of fear; and you, who were highly esteemed by them, will come to be held in contempt.

notes: Śaṅkara: they will think that he withdrew for fear of Karṇa and the others, not out of compassion.

sanskrit.deva:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥ ३६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ |
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim || 36 ||

lines.iast: nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
lines.deva: निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्

padaccheda.iast: avācya-vādān ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tava ahitāḥ nindantaḥ tava sāmarthyam tataḥ duḥkhataram nu kim
padaccheda.deva: अवाच्य-वादान् च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तव अहिताः निन्दन्तः तव सामर्थ्यम् ततः दुःखतरम् नु किम्

words.meaning: words not fit to be spoken

translations.text: Your enemies will say many things not fit to be spoken, deriding your prowess. What could be more painful than that?

sanskrit.deva:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥ ३७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ || 37 ||

lines.iast: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm
lines.deva: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्

padaccheda.iast: hataḥ vā prāpsyasi svargam jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm tasmāt uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: हतः वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गम् जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् तस्मात् उत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृत-निश्चयः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Slain, you will gain heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore arise, O son of Kuntī, resolved to fight.

notes: Śaṅkara: either way he gains. The resolve is: ‘I shall conquer the enemy, or I shall die.’

sanskrit.deva:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau |
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi || 38 ||

padaccheda.iast: sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābha-alābhau jaya-ajayau tataḥ yuddhāya yujyasva na evam pāpam avāpsyasi
padaccheda.deva: सुख-दुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभ-अलाभौ जय-अजयौ ततः युद्धाय युज्यस्व न एवम् पापम् अवाप्स्यसि

translations.text: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, make ready for battle. In this way you will incur no sin.

notes: Śaṅkara: to treat them alike is to have neither attachment nor aversion. This advice is given in passing, for one who is fighting because fighting is his own dharma.

sanskrit.deva:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु ।
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhir yoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu |
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi || 39 ||

lines.iast: eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhir yoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu
lines.deva: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु

lines.iast: buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
lines.deva: बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि

padaccheda.iast: eṣā te abhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiḥ yoge tu imām śṛṇu buddhyā yuktaḥ yayā pārtha karma-bandham prahāsyasi
padaccheda.deva: एषा ते अभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिः योगे तु इमाम् शृणु बुद्ध्या युक्तः यया पार्थ कर्म-बन्धम् प्रहास्यसि

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

words.meaning: in regard to the discernment of the truth

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: This understanding has been told to you in regard to the discernment of the truth. Now hear it in regard to yoga: endowed with this understanding, O Pārtha, you will cast off the bondage of action.

notes: Śaṅkara: sāṃkhya is the discernment of the supreme reality; the understanding concerning it is the knowledge that directly removes grief, delusion and the other causes of the cycle of birth and death. yoga is the means to it: the yoga of action, performed without attachment as worship of the Lord after giving up the pairs of opposites, and the yoga of absorption (samādhi). The bondage of action is action itself, as merit and demerit; it is cast off through the knowledge that comes by the Lord's grace.

sanskrit.deva:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥ ४० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nehābhikramanāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt || 40 ||

lines.iast: svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt

padaccheda.iast: na iha abhikrama-nāśaḥ asti pratyavāyaḥ na vidyate su-alpam api asya dharmasya trāyate mahataḥ bhayāt
padaccheda.deva: न इह अभिक्रम-नाशः अस्ति प्रत्यवायः न विद्यते सु-अल्पम् अपि अस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतः भयात्

words.meaning: loss of what has been begun

translations.text: Here nothing that has been begun is lost, and no contrary result follows. Even a little of this dharma saves one from great fear.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘here’: on the path to liberation, the yoga of action. A beginning in it is not wasted, as a beginning in farming may be, nor does harm come of it, as may happen with medical treatment. The great fear is the fear of the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit.deva:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥ ४१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana |
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām || 41 ||

padaccheda.iast: vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ ekā iha kuru-nandana bahu-śākhāḥ hi anantāḥ ca buddhayaḥ avyavasāyinām
padaccheda.deva: व्यवसाय-आत्मिका बुद्धिः एका इह कुरु-नन्दन बहु-शाखाः हि अनन्ताः च बुद्धयः अव्यवसायिनाम्

words.meaning: of the nature of firm resolve

translations.text: Here, O joy of the Kurus, the understanding that is resolute is one; but the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘here’: on the path to the highest good. The resolute understanding is one because it arises from a right means of knowledge, and it sets aside the many contrary notions. The irresolute are those without the discerning understanding that such a means of knowledge gives; through the spreading of their notions the cycle of birth and death goes on without end.

sanskrit.deva:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥ ४२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ |
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ || 42 ||

padaccheda.iast: yām imām puṣpitām vācam pravadanti a-vipaścitaḥ veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha na anyat asti iti vādinaḥ
padaccheda.deva: याम् इमाम् पुष्पिताम् वाचम् प्रवदन्ति अ-विपश्चितः वेद-वाद-रताः पार्थ न अन्यत् अस्ति इति वादिनः

words.meaning: who delight in the words of the Veda

translations.text: The undiscerning, O Pārtha, who delight in the words of the Veda and say that there is nothing else, utter this flowery speech:

notes: Śaṅkara: flowery: lovely like a tree in bloom, pleasant to hear. The ‘words of the Veda’ are its many passages of praise that set out results and the means to them. ‘Nothing else’: nothing other than rites, which are the means to heaven and such results.

sanskrit.deva:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् ।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥ ४३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām |
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati || 43 ||

padaccheda.iast: kāma-ātmānaḥ svarga-parāḥ janma-karma-phala-pradām kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulām bhoga-aiśvarya-gatim prati
padaccheda.deva: काम-आत्मानः स्वर्ग-पराः जन्म-कर्म-फल-प्रदाम् क्रिया-विशेष-बहुलाम् भोग-ऐश्वर्य-गतिम् प्रति

words.meaning: holding heaven to be the highest
which gives birth as the fruit of action
the gaining of enjoyment and power

translations.text: full of desire, holding heaven to be the highest goal, they utter speech that gives birth as the fruit of action, and is full of particular rites for gaining enjoyment and power.

notes: Śaṅkara: the words describing the speech go with ‘they utter’ in the previous verse. Uttering it, the deluded keep turning in the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit.deva:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām |
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate || 44 ||

padaccheda.iast: bhoga-aiśvarya-prasaktānām tayā apahṛta-cetasām vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
padaccheda.deva: भोग-ऐश्वर्य-प्रसक्तानाम् तया अपहृत-चेतसाम् व्यवसाय-आत्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते

words.meaning: of those attached to enjoyment and power

translations.text: In those who are attached to enjoyment and power, and whose minds are carried away by that speech, the resolute understanding does not form in the mind.

notes: Śaṅkara: samādhi here is the inner organ, the intellect, ‘that in which everything is placed for the person's experience’. The resolute understanding, whether of sāṃkhya or of yoga, does not arise in it.

sanskrit.deva:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।
निर्द्वंद्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ ४५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna |
nirdvaṃdvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān || 45 ||

padaccheda.iast: traiguṇya-viṣayāḥ vedāḥ nistraiguṇyaḥ bhava arjuna nirdvaṃdvaḥ nitya-sattva-sthaḥ niryogakṣemaḥ ātmavān
padaccheda.deva: त्रैगुण्य-विषयाः वेदाः निस्त्रैगुण्यः भव अर्जुन निर्द्वंद्वः नित्य-सत्त्व-स्थः निर्योगक्षेमः आत्मवान्

words.meaning: having the world of the three guṇas as their subject
free from the pairs of opposites

translations.text: The Vedas have the world of the three guṇas as their subject; be free from the three guṇas, O Arjuna: free from the pairs of opposites, always abiding in sattva, free from getting and keeping, and self-possessed.

notes: Śaṅkara: traiguṇya is the cycle of birth and death, which the Vedas set forth. To be free of it is to be without desire. The pairs of opposites are things that cause pleasure and pain, each with its contrary. yoga is acquiring what one has not; kṣema is guarding what one has; one whose chief concern they are can hardly strive for the good. ātmavān: vigilant. This is advice for one who is doing his own dharma.
The guṇas are the three constituents of Prakṛti (sattva, rajas and tamas), which the Gītā explains in later adhyāyas; the Sanskrit names are kept here.

sanskrit.deva:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके ।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥ ४६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake |
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ || 46 ||

padaccheda.iast: yāvān arthaḥ udapāne sarvataḥ saṃpluta-udake tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
padaccheda.deva: यावान् अर्थः उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुत-उदके तावान् सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः

translations.text: Whatever use there is in a well is all found where water floods on every side; in the same way, whatever use there is in all the Vedas is found for a brahmin who knows.

notes: Śaṅkara: whatever purpose, such as bathing and drinking, is served by wells and ponds is all contained in the purpose served by a flood of water. So the fruit of all the rites taught in the Vedas is contained in the fruit of knowledge that belongs to the brahmin, the renouncer who knows the supreme truth. Hence, until one is fit for the path of knowledge, one who is entitled to rites must perform them, though they are like the well and the pond.

sanskrit.deva:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ ४७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karmaphalaheturbhūr mā te saṅgo 'stvakarmaṇi || 47 ||

padaccheda.iast: karmaṇi eva adhikāraḥ te mā phaleṣu kadācana mā karma-phala-hetuḥ bhūḥ mā te saṅgaḥ astu akarmaṇi
padaccheda.deva: कर्मणि एव अधिकारः ते मा फलेषु कदाचन मा कर्म-फल-हेतुः भूः मा ते सङ्गः अस्तु अकर्मणि

words.meaning: one who brings about the fruit of action

translations.text: Your entitlement is to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not be one who brings about the fruit of action, and do not be attached to inaction.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘to action alone’, and not to the path of knowledge. Never, in any state, is there to be craving for the fruit of action. One who acts out of such craving becomes the cause of that fruit, which is rebirth. And he should not think, ‘if the fruit is not wanted, why act at all?’, and so grow fond of not acting.

sanskrit.deva:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनंजय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya |
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate || 48 ||

lines.iast: yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya
lines.deva: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनंजय

lines.iast: siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
lines.deva: सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते

padaccheda.iast: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgam tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya siddhi-asiddhyoḥ samaḥ bhūtvā sama-tvam yogaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: योग-स्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गम् त्यक्त्वा धनंजय सिद्धि-असिद्ध्योः समः भूत्वा सम-त्वम् योगः उच्यते

translations.text: Established in yoga, O Dhanaṃjaya, perform actions, giving up attachment and remaining the same in success and failure. Evenness is called yoga.

notes: Śaṅkara: actions are to be done for the Lord alone, giving up even the attachment of ‘may the Lord be pleased with me’. Success is the gaining of knowledge that comes from purity of mind when action is done without craving for its fruit; failure is the opposite.

sanskrit.deva:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनंजय ।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ ४९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanaṃjaya |
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ || 49 ||

padaccheda.iast: dūreṇa hi avaram karma buddhi-yogāt dhanaṃjaya buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ
padaccheda.deva: दूरेण हि अवरम् कर्म बुद्धि-योगात् धनंजय बुद्धौ शरणम् अन्विच्छ कृपणाः फल-हेतवः

words.meaning: to action joined with evenness of mind
those who act for the fruit

translations.text: Action done for its fruit, O Dhanaṃjaya, is far inferior to action joined with evenness of mind. Seek refuge in that understanding. Pitiable are those who act for the fruit.

notes: Śaṅkara: action done by one who seeks its fruit is inferior because it is a cause of birth and death. The understanding in which refuge is to be sought is that of yoga, or the understanding of sāṃkhya which ripens from it: one is to take refuge in knowledge of the supreme truth.

sanskrit.deva:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते ।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte |
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam || 50 ||

padaccheda.iast: buddhi-yuktaḥ jahāti iha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte tasmāt yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
padaccheda.deva: बुद्धि-युक्तः जहाति इह उभे सुकृत-दुष्कृते तस्मात् योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्

translations.text: One endowed with this understanding casts off both merit and demerit here in this world. Therefore strive for yoga: yoga is skill in action.

notes: Śaṅkara: he casts them off through purity of mind and the gaining of knowledge. The skill is this: evenness of mind in success and failure, with the mind given over to the Lord, while one is engaged in the actions that are one's own dharma. By that evenness, actions whose nature is to bind lose that nature.

sanskrit.deva:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ ५१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam || 51 ||

lines.iast: karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ
lines.deva: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः

padaccheda.iast: karma-jam buddhi-yuktāḥ hi phalam tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padam gacchanti anāmayam
padaccheda.deva: कर्म-जम् बुद्धि-युक्ताः हि फलम् त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः जन्म-बन्ध-विनिर्मुक्ताः पदम् गच्छन्ति अनामयम्

words.meaning: freed from the bondage of birth

translations.text: For the wise, endowed with this understanding, give up the fruit born of action; freed from the bondage of birth, they go to the state that is free from all ill.

notes: Śaṅkara: the fruit born of action is the gaining of bodies, wished for or not. Having become men of knowledge, they are freed from the bondage of birth while still living, and reach the highest state of Viṣṇu, called liberation. Or else, he adds, the ‘understanding’ spoken of from verse 49 onwards is the vision of the supreme truth itself, since it is said to remove merit and demerit directly.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ ५२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati |
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca || 52 ||

lines.iast: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
lines.deva: तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च

padaccheda.iast: yadā te moha-kalilam buddhiḥ vyatitariṣyati tadā gantāsi nirvedam śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
padaccheda.deva: यदा ते मोह-कलिलम् बुद्धिः व्यतितरिष्यति तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदम् श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च

words.meaning: towards what is yet to be heard

grammar.en: past passive participle n. gen. sg.

translations.text: When your understanding crosses beyond the mire of delusion, then you will come to dispassion towards what is yet to be heard and what has been heard.

notes: Śaṅkara: the mire is the confusion, of the nature of delusion, that clouds the discernment of the Self from what is not the Self and turns the mind towards objects. When the understanding has become very pure, what has been heard and what remains to be heard both appear fruitless.

sanskrit.deva:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ५३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
samādhāvacalā buddhis tadā yogamavāpsyasi || 53 ||

padaccheda.iast: śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā samādhau acalā buddhiḥ tadā yogam avāpsyasi
padaccheda.deva: श्रुति-विप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला समाधौ अचला बुद्धिः तदा योगम् अवाप्स्यसि

words.meaning: bewildered by what it has heard

translations.text: When your understanding, bewildered by all that it has heard, stands unmoving and steady in the Self, then you will attain yoga.

notes: Śaṅkara: the mind is scattered by hearing the many texts that set out ends and means, some urging action and some withdrawal. samādhi here is the Self, ‘that in which the mind is settled’. The yoga then attained is the absorption that is discerning wisdom.

sanskrit.deva:
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥ ५४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava |
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim || 54 ||

lines.iast: sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
lines.deva: स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्

padaccheda.iast: sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhi-sthasya keśava sthita-dhīḥ kim prabhāṣeta kim āsīta vrajeta kim
padaccheda.deva: स्थित-प्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधि-स्थस्य केशव स्थित-धीः किम् प्रभाषेत किम् आसीत व्रजेत किम्

words.meaning: of the one whose wisdom is firm

translations.text: Arjuna said: What is the description, O Keśava, of one whose wisdom is firm, who is established in absorption? How would one of firm understanding speak, how would he sit, how would he walk?

notes: Śaṅkara: sthitaprajña is one in whom the wisdom ‘I am the supreme Brahman’ is firmly established. bhāṣā: how is he spoken of by others? The verse asks for the marks of such a person. From here to the end of the adhyāya these marks are taught, and they are also the means, to be won by effort, for one who seeks that state.

sanskrit.deva:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān |
ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñas tadocyate || 55 ||

lines.iast: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān

padaccheda.iast: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manaḥ-gatān ātmani eva ātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthita-prajñaḥ tadā ucyate
padaccheda.deva: प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनः-गतान् आत्मनि एव आत्मना तुष्टः स्थित-प्रज्ञः तदा उच्यते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: The Blessed Lord said: When a man gives up completely all the desires that have entered the mind, O Pārtha, and is content in the Self alone by the Self, then he is called one of firm wisdom.

notes: Śaṅkara: content in the inward Self by himself alone, looking to no outward gain, satisfied by the nectar of seeing the supreme truth. The wisdom is that born of discerning the Self from what is not the Self. Such a one is the renouncer who has given up the desire for sons, wealth and worlds, and delights in the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ |
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate || 56 ||

padaccheda.iast: duḥkheṣu anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīḥ muniḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: दुःखेषु अनुद्विग्न-मनाः सुखेषु विगत-स्पृहः वीत-राग-भय-क्रोधः स्थित-धीः मुनिः उच्यते

words.meaning: free from attachment, fear and anger

translations.text: One whose mind is not shaken in sorrows, who is free from longing in pleasures, and free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of firm understanding.

notes: Śaṅkara: his longing does not grow with pleasures as fire grows when fuel is added. The muni is the renouncer.

sanskrit.deva:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् ।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham |
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 57 ||

lines.iast: nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
lines.deva: नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ sarvatra anabhisnehaḥ tat tat prāpya śubha-aśubham na abhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
padaccheda.deva: यः सर्वत्र अनभिस्नेहः तत् तत् प्राप्य शुभ-अशुभम् न अभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who is without attachment everywhere, who neither rejoices nor hates on meeting with this or that, good or evil: his wisdom is firmly established.

notes: Śaṅkara: without attachment even to the body and to life.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 58 ||

padaccheda.iast: yadā saṃharate ca ayam kūrmaḥ aṅgāni iva sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇi indriya-arthebhyaḥ tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
padaccheda.deva: यदा संहरते च अयम् कूर्मः अङ्गानि इव सर्वशः इन्द्रियाणि इन्द्रिय-अर्थेभ्यः तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

words.meaning: from the objects of the senses

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: When he draws in his senses from their objects on every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, his wisdom is firmly established.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘he’ is the ascetic who has entered on the path of knowledge; the tortoise draws in its limbs out of fear.

sanskrit.deva:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
rasavarjaṃ raso 'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate || 59 ||

padaccheda.iast: viṣayāḥ vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ rasa-varjam rasaḥ api asya param dṛṣṭvā nivartate
padaccheda.deva: विषयाः विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः रस-वर्जम् रसः अपि अस्य परम् दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते

words.meaning: from one who does not feed on them

translations.text: The objects of sense turn away from an embodied being who does not feed on them, but the taste for them remains. Even that taste turns away from him when he has seen the supreme.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘objects’ here stands for the senses, which withdraw even in a foolish man who practises hard austerity and takes in no objects; the subtle liking for objects is not thereby given up. rasa is well known in the sense of attachment. It ceases for the ascetic who has realised the supreme truth, Brahman, and abides as ‘I am that’. Without right vision the liking is not rooted out; so the wisdom that is right vision must be made firm.

sanskrit.deva:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥ ६० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ || 60 ||

padaccheda.iast: yatataḥ hi api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabham manaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यततः हि अपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभम् मनः

translations.text: For the turbulent senses, O son of Kuntī, carry away by force the mind even of a discerning man who is striving.

notes: Śaṅkara: so one who would make right vision firm must first bring the senses under control. They agitate a man who turns towards objects, and then carry off his mind openly, even while he looks on with discernment.

sanskrit.deva:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ |
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 61 ||

lines.iast: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ
lines.deva: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः

lines.iast: vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
lines.deva: वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

padaccheda.iast: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yuktaḥ āsīta mad-paraḥ vaśe hi yasya indriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
padaccheda.deva: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्तः आसीत मद्-परः वशे हि यस्य इन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

words.meaning: holding me to be the highest

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: Having restrained them all, one should sit collected, holding me to be the highest; for he whose senses are under control has wisdom that is firmly established.

notes: Śaṅkara: matpara: one for whom ‘I, Vāsudeva, the inward Self of all, am the highest’; he should sit thinking ‘I am not other than he’. The senses come under control by the strength of practice.

sanskrit.deva:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate |
saṅgātsaṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho 'bhijāyate || 62 ||

padaccheda.iast: dhyāyataḥ viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgaḥ teṣu upajāyate saṅgāt saṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodhaḥ abhijāyate
padaccheda.deva: ध्यायतः विषयान् पुंसः सङ्गः तेषु उपजायते सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात् क्रोधः अभिजायते

translations.text: When a man dwells in thought on the objects of sense, attachment to them arises. From attachment desire is born, and from desire anger springs up.

notes: Śaṅkara: this and the next verse give the root of every evil for one who is on the way to ruin. Anger arises from desire when desire is thwarted by something. Attachment (saṅga) is fondness for the objects; desire (kāma) is thirst.

sanskrit.deva:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥ ६३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
krodhādbhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ |
smṛtibhraṃśādbuddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati || 63 ||

padaccheda.iast: krodhāt bhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ smṛti-bhraṃśāt buddhi-nāśaḥ buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati
padaccheda.deva: क्रोधात् भवति संमोहः संमोहात् स्मृति-विभ्रमः स्मृति-भ्रंशात् बुद्धि-नाशः बुद्धि-नाशात् प्रणश्यति

translations.text: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, the failing of memory; from the loss of memory, the ruin of understanding; and from the ruin of understanding he perishes.

notes: Śaṅkara: delusion is the failure to discern what ought and ought not to be done: an angry man abuses even his teacher. The memory that fails is that formed by the teaching of scripture and teacher; it does not arise when the occasion for it comes. The ruin of understanding is the unfitness of the mind to tell right from wrong. A man is a man only so long as his mind is fit for this; he ‘perishes’ in that he becomes unfit for any human end.

sanskrit.deva:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran |
ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati || 64 ||

padaccheda.iast: rāga-dveṣa-viyuktaiḥ tu viṣayān indriyaiḥ caran ātma-vaśyaiḥ vidheya-ātmā prasādam adhigacchati
padaccheda.deva: राग-द्वेष-वियुक्तैः तु विषयान् इन्द्रियैः चरन् आत्म-वश्यैः विधेय-आत्मा प्रसादम् अधिगच्छति

translations.text: But one whose mind is obedient, who moves among objects with senses that are freed from attachment and aversion and are under his own control, attains serenity.

notes: Śaṅkara: now the cause of liberation is told. The senses naturally act from attachment and aversion; the seeker of liberation experiences, with senses free of these, only the objects that cannot be avoided. prasāda is clearness, well-being.

sanskrit.deva:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate |
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate || 65 ||

padaccheda.iast: prasāde sarva-duḥkhānām hāniḥ asya upajāyate prasanna-cetasaḥ hi āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
padaccheda.deva: प्रसादे सर्व-दुःखानाम् हानिः अस्य उपजायते प्रसन्न-चेतसः हि आशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते

words.meaning: of one whose mind is serene

translations.text: In serenity all his sorrows come to an end; for the understanding of one whose mind is serene quickly becomes steady.

notes: Śaṅkara: the understanding settles on every side, like space; it becomes unmoving as the very nature of the Self. Therefore one should deal, with senses free of attachment and aversion, only with unavoidable objects that scripture does not forbid.

sanskrit.deva:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ ६६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā |
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham || 66 ||

lines.iast: na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham

padaccheda.iast: na asti buddhiḥ ayuktasya na ca ayuktasya bhāvanā na ca abhāvayataḥ śāntiḥ a-śāntasya kutaḥ sukham
padaccheda.deva: न अस्ति बुद्धिः अयुक्तस्य न च अयुक्तस्य भावना न च अभावयतः शान्तिः अ-शान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्

words.meaning: for one who is not collected
for one who is not collected
for one who does not contemplate

translations.text: There is no understanding for one who is not collected, and no contemplation; without contemplation there is no peace; and for one without peace, how can there be happiness?

notes: Śaṅkara: the understanding is that which has the nature of the Self for its object; bhāvanā is steady application to the knowledge of the Self. Happiness is the turning of the senses away from the thirst for enjoying objects; that thirst is sorrow itself.
abhāvayataḥ is a causative present participle with a-; it is labelled here as a present participle.

sanskrit.deva:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥ ६७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano 'nuvidhīyate |
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi || 67 ||

padaccheda.iast: indriyāṇām hi caratām yat manaḥ anuvidhīyate tat asya harati prajñām vāyuḥ nāvam iva ambhasi
padaccheda.deva: इन्द्रियाणाम् हि चरताम् यत् मनः अनुविधीयते तत् अस्य हरति प्रज्ञाम् वायुः नावम् इव अम्भसि

translations.text: For the mind that follows after the roaming senses carries away his wisdom, as the wind carries away a boat on the water.

notes: Śaṅkara: the wisdom is that born of discerning the Self from what is not the Self. As the wind drives a boat off its course, so the mind takes wisdom from the Self and turns it to objects.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā || 68 ||

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt yasya mahā-bāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇi indriya-arthebhyaḥ tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् यस्य महा-बाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः इन्द्रियाणि इन्द्रिय-अर्थेभ्यः तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. pl.

words.meaning: from the objects of the senses

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: Therefore, O mighty-armed, he whose senses are held back in every way from their objects has wisdom that is firmly established.

notes: Śaṅkara: this sums up what was argued in several ways from verse 60.

sanskrit.deva:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥ ६९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ || 69 ||

lines.iast: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī
lines.deva: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी

lines.iast: yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
lines.deva: यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः

padaccheda.iast: yā niśā sarva-bhūtānām tasyām jāgarti saṃyamī yasyām jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyataḥ muneḥ
padaccheda.deva: या निशा सर्व-भूतानाम् तस्याम् जागर्ति संयमी यस्याम् जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतः मुनेः

translations.text: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; and that in which beings are awake is night for the sage who sees.

notes: Śaṅkara: the ‘night’ of all beings is the supreme truth, the object of the one of firm wisdom: to the ignorant it is dark, as day is to creatures of the night. The self-controlled yogī has awakened in it from the sleep of ignorance. That in which beings are said to be awake is the night of ignorance, with its division into knower and known, in which they are really asleep, like dreamers.
Śaṅkara: hence rites are enjoined only in the state of ignorance, not in the state of knowledge. He concludes that the knower of the Self is entitled only to the renunciation of all action.

sanskrit.deva:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī || 70 ||

lines.iast: tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
lines.deva: तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी

padaccheda.iast: āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭham samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat tadvat kāmāḥ yam praviśanti sarve saḥ śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī
padaccheda.deva: आपूर्यमाणम् अचल-प्रतिष्ठम् समुद्रम् आपः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् तद्वत् कामाः यम् प्रविशन्ति सर्वे सः शान्तिम् आप्नोति न काम-कामी

words.meaning: one who desires the objects of desire

translations.text: As waters enter the ocean, which is being filled yet stays unmoved, so he whom all desires enter attains peace; not so one who desires the objects of desire.

notes: Śaṅkara: the waters enter the ocean without changing it. So desires, even in the presence of their objects, enter such a man without disturbing him; they dissolve in the Self and do not bring him under their sway. The peace he attains is liberation.

sanskrit.deva:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ |
nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati || 71 ||

padaccheda.iast: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumān carati niḥspṛhaḥ nirmamaḥ nirahaṃkāraḥ saḥ śāntim adhigacchati
padaccheda.deva: विहाय कामान् यः सर्वान् पुमान् चरति निःस्पृहः निर्ममः निरहंकारः सः शान्तिम् अधिगच्छति

translations.text: The man who abandons all desires and moves about free from longing, without the sense of ‘mine’ and without the sense of ‘I’, attains peace.

notes: Śaṅkara: he is the renouncer, whose only activity is what keeps the body alive, and who longs not even for that. nirmama: without the notion ‘this is mine’ even of the few things needed for life. nirahaṃkāra: without self-regard on account of learning and the like. The peace is the end of all the sorrow of worldly existence, called nirvāṇa: he becomes Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ ७२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
sthitvāsyāmantakāle 'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati || 72 ||

lines.iast: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati
lines.deva: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति

padaccheda.iast: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha na enām prāpya vimuhyati sthitvā asyām anta-kāle api brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati
padaccheda.deva: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ न एनाम् प्राप्य विमुह्यति स्थित्वा अस्याम् अन्त-काले अपि ब्रह्म-निर्वाणम् ऋच्छति

translations.text: This is the state of Brahman, O Pārtha. Having attained it, one is no longer deluded. Abiding in it even at the last hour, one attains the bliss of Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara: the state of Brahman is to renounce all action and abide as Brahman. brahmanirvāṇa is the bliss of Brahman, liberation. If even one who reaches this state in the last stage of life attains it, how much more one who renounces straight from the student's life and abides in Brahman as long as he lives.
